definitions.explanation: The area surrounding a city, typically residential or semi-rural districts outside the urban center.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}{近郊|きんこう}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in the suburbs of Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {近郊|きんこう}の{農家|のうか}から{新鮮|しんせん}な{野菜|やさい}を{仕入|しい}れている。
examples.english: We source fresh vegetables from farms in the suburbs.

examples.japanese: {都心|としん}から{近郊|きんこう}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す{家族|かぞく}が{増|ふ}えており、{通勤|つうきん}ラッシュがますます{深刻|しんこく}になっている。
examples.english: More families are moving to the suburbs, and rush-hour commuting is becoming increasingly severe.

notes:
Compound of {近|きん} (near) + {郊|こう} (outskirts). Not to be confused with the homophone {均衡|きんこう} (balance, equilibrium).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {都市|とし}{近郊|きんこう} (city outskirts)
- {近郊|きんこう}{農業|のうぎょう} (suburban agriculture)
- {近郊|きんこう}に{住|す}む (to live in the suburbs)

USAGE:
Typically used with larger city names: {東京|とうきょう}{近郊|きんこう}, {大阪|おおさか}{近郊|きんこう}. Similar to {郊外|こうがい} (suburbs), but {近郊|きんこう} emphasizes proximity to the city center, while {郊外|こうがい} focuses on being outside the city proper.
